definitions.explanation: The polite form of {餅|もち} (mochi), a traditional Japanese food made from glutinous rice that has been pounded into a sticky, chewy mass. A staple of New Year celebrations and used in many traditional sweets and dishes.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: To eat mochi at New Year's.

examples.japanese: お{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}いて→焼く：01123_yaku⟧⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけた→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧。
examples.english: I grilled the mochi and dipped it in soy sauce.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、お{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{喉|のど}→喉：00977_nodo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{詰|つ}まらせる→詰まる：02079_tsumaru⟧⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ニュース→ニュース：04437_nyuusu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{報道|ほうどう}→報道：04438_houdou⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Every New Year, there are news reports about accidents where people choke on mochi.

examples.japanese: ⟦おばあちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{臼|うす}→臼：26038_usu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{杵|きね}→杵：26037_kine⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧お{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ついて⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: Grandma pounded mochi for us with a mortar and pestle.

notes:
The polite お prefix is standard with ⟦{餅|もち}→餅：03900_mochi⟧ in everyday speech, making お{餅|もち} the default conversational form. The お is not merely decorative; dropping it can sound curt in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つく: to pound mochi
- お{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧: to grill/toast mochi
- お{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{煮|に}る→煮る：01971_niru⟧: to boil mochi (in soup)
- ⟦{切|き}り{餅|もち}→切り餅：24896_kirimochi⟧: pre-cut mochi blocks (sold in packages)
- {丸|まる}{餅|もち}: round mochi (Kansai style)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Mochi is deeply associated with ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧ (New Year). It appears in ⟦{雑煮|ぞうに}→雑煮：14581_zouni⟧ (New Year's soup), ⟦{鏡餅|かがみもち}→鏡餅：19469_kagamimochi⟧ (decorative stacked mochi), and {磯辺焼|いそべや}き (grilled mochi wrapped in nori). The shape varies by region: round in western Japan, rectangular in eastern Japan. Every January, Japanese media report on choking incidents (⟦{窒息|ちっそく}→窒息：16495_chissoku⟧⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧) among elderly people, making mochi safety a recurring seasonal topic.
